title: Liver disease: cirrhosis, hepatitis C, fatty liver
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's liver disease.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for liver disease.

HPI: The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation of his chronic liver condition. He reports that he has been experiencing increasing abdominal girth and a feeling of fullness. He notes that his fatigue has been persistent over the last month. He states that he successfully ceased all alcohol consumption several months ago and remains sober. He reports no new episodes of fever, chills, or acute pain. He denies any recent changes in his mental status or significant weight loss.

Medication List:
- Spironolactone 25 mg daily
- Lactulose 30 mL three times daily
- Vitamin K 10 mg daily

Vitals:
BP: 132/78 mmHg
HR: 74 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 185 lbs

Recent Labs:
AST: 88 U/L
ALT: 72 U/L
Albumin: 2.8 g/dL
INR: 1.4
Platelets: 110,000/uL
Bilirubin: 1.8 mg/dL
eGFR: 55 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, or night sweats.
Gastrointestinal: Reports increased abdominal girth. Denies nausea, vomiting, or black stools.
Neurological: Denies confusion or tremors.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain.

Social History: Retired. Lives with his wife. He no longer drinks alcohol.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Abdomen: Significant distension noted. Firm, non-tender. Palpable fluid waves present.
Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities.

Assessment:
The patient is an 86-year-old male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis. He currently presents with worsening ascites. His laboratory values show a decline in albumin and a slight elevation in INR, consistent with his chronic condition. He has successfully maintained sobriety.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Monitor for signs of infection or worsening fluid accumulation.
3. Follow up in four weeks for a repeat laboratory panel and clinical reassessment.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
